idiom_name: hand-written dispatch table with a guard callback chain
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the base action becomes a dispatch table: every operation is a function-pointer entry that is only ever invoked through one shared dispatch function, and the shared security sequence lives there as a guard chain (authenticate, authorize, validate session, validate input, audit) built from function pointers plus an explicit request context. The pattern survives as structure plus discipline: the dispatcher is the single entry point, the guards are the reusable security components, and the action functions contain business logic only. Keep the guard table immutable after startup and pass request-scoped state through the context struct rather than globals.
pitfalls: Without a single dispatcher every entry point re-implements the guard sequence; the language offers no inheritance or decorators to enforce coverage.
A guard table shared across threads must be immutable after startup; keep per-request state in the context struct instead of file-scope variables.
The void* context traded for genericity loses type safety: a wrong cast inside a guard is undefined behaviour that ordinary tests may not trigger.
